name: Choledochal Cysts

criteria.description: Identification of cystic dilatation of the bile ducts on imaging (ultrasound, MRCP, or ERCP)
Presence of abdominal pain, jaundice, or palpable mass
Exclusion of other causes of biliary obstruction such as choledocholithiasis or malignancy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Imaging confirmation of bile duct cystic dilatation plus exclusion of other causes of biliary obstruction
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Classification of cyst type is based on Todani system which guides management

pathognomonic.symptomName: Palpable right upper quadrant abdominal mass

rare.notes: Usually occurs in adulthood as a late complication

laboratory: Elevated liver function tests (alkaline phosphatase, gamma-glutamyl transferase, bilirubin)
Elevated serum amylase/lipase if pancreatitis present
imaging: Ultrasound showing cystic dilatation of bile ducts
Magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP) demonstrating cyst morphology and extent
Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) for detailed ductal anatomy
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; considered congenital malformation
other: Histopathology may show inflammation, fibrosis, or dysplasia in cyst wall
Risk of malignant transformation especially in untreated cysts

distinguishingFeatures: Absence or obliteration of extrahepatic bile ducts
Presence of gallstones in bile ducts
Intermittent biliary colic without cystic dilatation
Imaging shows stones rather than cystic structures

redFlags: Sudden onset of severe abdominal pain with fever and jaundice (acute cholangitis)
Signs of malignant transformation such as weight loss, persistent jaundice, or worsening liver function
references: Todani T, Watanabe Y, Narusue M, Tabuchi K, Okajima K. Congenital bile duct cysts: classification, operative procedures, and review of thirty-seven cases including cancer arising from choledochal cyst. Am J Surg. 1977 Nov;134(5):263-9.
Khandelwal C, et al. Choledochal cysts: a review of literature. Indian J Radiol Imaging. 2013;23(3):264-272.
Yamaguchi M. Congenital choledochal cyst: analysis of 143 cases including cancer arising from choledochal cyst. Am J Surg. 1980 Sep;140(3):653-7.
